groups.label: Relative Clauses (Defining & Non-Defining)
groups.definition: Clauses introduced by who, which, that, where, or whose to add information about a noun.
rules: Defining (no commas): essential info (The man who lives next door is a doctor).
Non-defining (with commas): extra info (My brother, who lives in Paris, is an architect).
Whose: expresses possession (A writer whose book won an award).

examples.t: The woman who called you is my supervisor.
London, which is the capital of the UK, is very historic.

groups.label: Conditionals (Zero, First, Second, Third)
groups.definition: Expressing conditions and outcomes across real and hypothetical situations.
rules: Zero: If + Present Simple, Present Simple (general truths).
First: If + Present Simple, WILL + Base Verb (real future possibility).
Second: If + Past Simple, WOULD + Base Verb (unreal present/future).
Third: If + Past Perfect, WOULD HAVE + V3 (unreal past regret).

examples.t: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.
If I had more time, I would travel more.
